$comment: Accepted duplicated lines per file pair, plus generated files whose duplication is the generator's output shape. Each `pairs` value is {"lines": N, "reason": "…"}: the reason is mandatory and says why this duplication stays, or starts with `TODO: ` when it should be extracted and the reason says how. `pnpm check jscpd-rust` shrink-wraps the numbers, so a reason is the only part written by hand. See `scripts/check/checks/DETAILS.md § Allowlist consent`.

exempt.apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/intl/shipped_: generated by apps/desktop/scripts/gen-shipped-locales.ts; the `zh` and `zh-Hant` entries carry the same CLDR `region_scripts` data because that is what CLDR says, so the clone tracks the shipped-locale table and no extraction can remove it

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/about/platfor.reason: Per-OS answer sheets for "Tell me about this": `platform/mod.rs` swaps in exactly one file per OS (`cfg_attr(path = ...)`), and each file is the complete list of what that OS answers. The shared stretch is `download_record`'s tail plus three one-line stubs (`last_opened` and `default_app` answer `NoRecord`, `signature` answers `NoCodeSigningOnThisOs`) that happen to agree on Linux and Windows today. A shared stub module re-exported into both would save a dozen trivial lines but make a reader chase a second file to learn what an OS says, and it would need its own `cfg` to stay unused on macOS. Windows isn't a target yet, so these answers diverge the day it becomes one. Revisit if a third non-macOS OS lands with the same stubs.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/agent/store/m.reason: `read_schema_version`, the `prepare_cached` plus `query_map` plus absent-means-zero match each durable store uses to read its own `meta` table, typed to `AgentStoreError` in one copy and `OperationLogStoreError` in the other, with `stamp_schema_version` and `bootstrap_meta` sitting beside it in the same shape. The two ladders are deliberately separate copies of one tiny mechanism so that neither durable DB's schema discipline can be changed by editing the other's helper, a decision recorded in `agent/store/DETAILS.md` § Why a second durable DB, mirroring the operation log, which names the duplicated `token_enum!` macro as the same call. Revisit if a third durable store lands and all three can agree on one error type.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/file_system/t.reason: The two batched xattr reads (Finder tags read per volume group, then re-read for the verify pass): each hands its group's wire paths to `read_xattr_many`, and the trait's flip to app paths (#1225) spread the bridged batch (`.map(|p| AppPath::legacy_unchecked(p).into_owned())`) over enough lines to reach the clone floor. It goes when the app's tag paths are app paths (milestone 10c): the batch is then handed on as is.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/menu/context_.reason: TODO: #1178. `cmdr_about::gather` is the context menu's grace-then-late engine made generic over the job key and the answer (`crates/cmdr-about/DETAILS.md` § The gathering engine), so `deliver` and `collect` (the pending removal, the `ready` / `late` switch under the delivery lock, the deadline wait loop) match line for line. Move the menu onto one shared engine so a grace, cancel, or late-answer fix lands once: either lift `gather.rs` into a small tauri-free crate both depend on (the menu shouldn't depend on the fact-card crate for a threading primitive), or have `context_menu_facts.rs` key the generic `Gathering<FactKind, Fact>` by its fact kind and keep only `FactsRequest`, `GRACE`, its pool config, and `Slow<T>`. The menu's tests keep running on plain threads.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/network/os_mo.reason: The assertion tail of two parser tests, one per share-listing CLI (`parse_smbclient_output` and `parse_smbutil_output`), each fed a fixture in that tool's own column layout; the assertions spell out the shared `ShareInfo` contract (four disk shares survive, `IPC$` and `ADMIN$` are filtered, a missing comment reads as `None`). An `assert_nas_shares` helper would need a test-support module reachable from both files and would move the expectations away from the fixture that produces them, so a red run would name a helper line instead of the case that broke.

crates/cmdr-adb/src/volume/mutation.rs ↔.reason: `PatchSource` trait boilerplate, not logic: the volume id, the listing host, `patch_stat` forwarding to the backend's own stat, and `patch_display_path` / `patch_app_path` forwarding to its `paths.rs` translation. The patching itself is already shared (`cmdr_fs::volume::patching`). With the app-path conversion (#1225) both backends' impls lost their bridge preludes and came out token-identical. Same trade as the `volume_impl.rs` pairs: a macro emitting trait methods costs more lines than it removes and hides them from `codegraph_search` and go-to-definition. `patch_display_path` goes when the trait drops its `std::path` form, which shrinks this pair.

crates/cmdr-adb/src/volume/volume_impl.r.reason: `Volume` trait-method signatures delegating in one line, in five blocks: `list_directory*`, the read path (`open_read_stream*`, `read_range`), the write path's `create_*`, `delete` / `rename`, and `notify_mutation` beside the three `scan_for_*`. Every body is `self.noting(self.*_impl(..))` or a call straight into `cmdr_fs::volume` (`patching`, `scan_walk`). The app-path conversion (#1225) removed ADB's bridge preludes, which had kept the bodies apart since WebDAV converted. Same trade as the `cmdr-sftp` ↔ `cmdr-webdav` entry: a macro emitting trait methods costs more lines than it removes and hides every one from `codegraph_search` and go-to-definition. Revisit when a body stops being a one-line delegation, or when enough backends land that the macro pays for itself.

crates/cmdr-fs/src/metadata/platform/was.reason: TODO: windows-port plan tasks 35 and 36. Windows' metadata arm is honest stubs today (no mode, xattrs, ACL, flags, or removal blockers: `NotApplicable`, `Free`, empty), which read line for line like the browser build's arm, whose answers are final. Each stub gets its real Windows body in those tasks (the read-only attribute, alternate data streams, the DACL, Hidden and Locked as attributes), and the pair stops matching one class at a time. Sharing a "no metadata" module now would tie a final answer to a placeholder and be undone class by class.

crates/cmdr-fs/src/volume/conformance/me.reason: Two contract cases' shared fixture setup (assert the folder is absent, create it, write one file into it): the trait's flip to app paths (#1225) bridged each `Volume` call (`&AppPath::legacy_unchecked(dir)`), and rustfmt's longer lines made the two setups token-identical. The bridges go when `cmdr-fs` speaks app paths internally (milestone 5); if the setup still matches then, extract it into a conformance helper.

crates/cmdr-git/src/volume.rs ↔ crates/c.reason: `Volume` trait boilerplate shared by the two routed read-only views (`GitPortalVolume`, `ResticVolume`): `scan_for_copy` and `scan_for_copy_batch_with_boundary`, each a one-line delegation to `cmdr_fs::volume::scan_walk`, then the `routes_over_a_parent() == true` capability flag under the same section banner. Same trade as the backend `volume_impl.rs` pairs: folding them takes a macro that emits trait methods, which costs more lines than it removes and hides them from `codegraph_search` and go-to-definition. Revisit when a body stops being a one-line delegation. The `Volume` trait's flip to app paths (#1225) grew it: each flipped method gained the same two-line bridge prelude (`let path_std = path.as_std_legacy(); let path: &Path = &path_std;`) or bridged argument, which made neighbouring trait methods token-identical across backends. Those go as each crate converts (milestones 5–10e).

crates/cmdr-index/src/importance/writer..reason: TODO: `run_wal_checkpoint` in `importance/writer.rs` and in `media_index/writer/maintenance.rs` are identical apart from the `log::` target, down to the 250 ms busy timeout, the restore to 5000 ms, and the four-arm match on the returned `(busy, log_size, checkpointed)` row; the media copy's own doc comment says it mirrors the importance one. Add a crate-private `crates/cmdr-index/src/sqlite_wal.rs` beside `fingerprint.rs` exposing `pub(crate) fn checkpoint_truncate(conn: &Connection, log_target: &'static str)`, and leave each writer a one-line call plus its own doc comment about why its workload needs the truncate. `indexing/writer/maintenance.rs`'s `handle_wal_checkpoint` stays separate: it carries a busy handler and an `IndexFailureSignal`, so it is a different function that happens to run the same pragma.

crates/cmdr-index/src/indexing/network_s.reason: The `use` block, nothing else. Two sibling scanners in `network_scanner/` reach for the same 17 imports (`VecDeque`, `FuturesUnordered`, `cmdr_fs::volume::Volume`, `super::ScanPacer`, `BATCH_SIZE`, the `LogPrivate` markers, and the rest), because a full scan and a reconcile scan walk the same trait with the same pacing. Rust makes every file spell its own imports out, so there is nothing here to extract.

crates/cmdr-index/src/indexing/reconcile.reason: Both ends sit inside `#[cfg(test)] mod bench`, the `#[ignore]`d reconcile performance guard that never runs in CI. The block is phase A of the measurement (per dir: `list_children_on`, build the `by_name` map, `black_box` it), repeated byte for byte in `reconcile_noop_messages` and `reconcile_noop_single_aggregate` so the two arms' `diff(read)` numbers compare directly, and each arm reads as the literal message stream it models, which is what lets a reader check it against `reconciler.rs`.

crates/cmdr-index/src/media_index/networ.reason: TODO: the per-image decision ladder shared by `run_sequential` and `run_parallel`'s dispatcher: the cancel and idle checks, `os_join`, the `is_excluded` / `should_enrich` skip, the `done` and `bytes_done` bump, and the `needs_enrichment` / `needs_clip` staleness pair. Extract a pure `fn classify_image(...) -> ImageStep` beside them, with `ImageStep::{Pause(PauseReason), Skip, Enrich { want_vision, want_clip, os_path }}`, and let each arm keep only its own exit shape: the sequential one returns `finish_paused(...)`, the dispatcher sets `reason` and breaks so it can join its workers. Which images a pass touches and when it pauses is the data-safety contract written in `network/CLAUDE.md`, so the two arms agreeing should be a property of the code rather than of two copies staying in step.

crates/cmdr-listing-wasm/src/operations_.reason: `OperationVolumes` trait-method signatures with constant bodies: the browser demo's `DemoVolumes` and the engine's test-only `NoOperationVolumes` both answer "no archive or git-portal routes" (`routes_over_its_parent`, `path_is_inside_archive`, `path_crosses_archive_boundary`, `forget_archive_index`). crates/cmdr-operations/src/rename/bulk.r.reason: `rotate_local_cycle` and `rotate_remote_cycle`: the cycle-breaking rotation (move the first row aside to a unique temp, rename the rest in reverse order, land the temp on the first destination, and restore the half-rotation on any failure).
